title: A Competitor Price-Match Beyond the Retired Discount Cap
scenario_text:
A deal desk analyst at Mowbray Retail must decide how to handle a competitor price-match request, given how a comparable request was handled last year.

**Decision A (2023-11)**
Customer 'Harlow Group' | new business | requested a 35% competitor price-match discount. The regional Sales Director approved it directly. Note at the time: 'Directors may approve competitor price-matches up to 40% at their discretion.'

**Current request C (2024-08-15)**
Customer 'Padstow Group' | new business | requesting a 35% competitor price-match discount, with a competitor quote attached. The AE has cited the Harlow approval as supporting evidence.

**Discount Authority Policy (current, effective 2024-04-01)**
Competitor price-matches up to 20% may be approved by a Sales Director. Price-matches above 20% now require VP Sales approval, and price-matches above 30% additionally require a verified competitor quote on file. The prior director-discretion authority for price-matches up to 40% was retired when this policy took effect. VP exceptions remain available up to 40% with the required documentation.

**Slack — #deal-desk**
AE: 'Harlow got a 35% match last year on the Director's sign-off, so Padstow should just get the same. Let's not overcomplicate it.'
Analyst: 'Harlow closed in November — before the April discount policy. Let me confirm who can actually approve a 35% match now.'

The AE wants to close this week and is asking the analyst to grant the 35% match under the Director's authority. A verified competitor quote is attached to Padstow's deal.
question: How should the analyst handle Padstow Group's 35% competitor price-match request?
choices: Grant the 35% price-match under the Sales Director's authority, citing the Harlow Group approval as established precedent.

Route the 35% price-match to VP Sales for approval with the verified competitor quote on file, because the Harlow approval predates the April 1, 2024 policy that retired director discretion above 20%.
Offer a 20% price-match instead, so the discount stays within the Sales Director's current authority and avoids VP escalation.
Deny the price-match, since competitor matches above 30% are no longer permitted at Mowbray Retail.
